full_judgment: 3. Defendant Government of Bangladesh contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations and stating, inter alia, that the suit is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and is not maintainable; that the defendant government further denied that the Dhaka Court of Wards Estate settled the suit plot to the plaintiff No. by granting amalnama or rent receipt on receipt of salami or that the plaintiff No. 1 leased out some portions of the suit plot to some tenants and the suit land remained in his possession or that the plaintiff No. 1 gifted some portion of the suit property to plaintiff Nos. 2-5 or that the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing the same peacefully. The further case of the defendant Government is that the suit plot was declared as reserved forest under Gazette Notification No. 3125 dated 13.4.55 published in the Dhaka Gazette on 5th May, 1965 and subsequently the Nowab Estate was acquired by the Government under the provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Since the aforesaid Gazette Notification suit plot is in peaceful possession of the Forest Department. The Exlandlord of Dhaka Nawab Estate entered into an agreement with the Collector of Mymensingh and Dhaka on 26.1.1923 for the management of the forest and as such ex-landlord had no right to settle the suit plot to the plaintiff No. 1. The suit plot having been correctly recorded in the name of the Forest Department in the SA and RS Khatian, the suit is barred under section 144B of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The plaintiffs in order to grab the forest land of the Government have filed the suit on the basis of forged, fabricated, ante-dated and fraudulent papers. The plaintiffs did not acquire any right, title, interest or possession in the suit land on the basis of the alleged amalnama and rent receipt.
